newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Energy says high crude costs cut profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan Energy says high crude costs cut profits.

text.p: Japan Energy Corp, a leading oil company, blamed surging crude oil prices and a weak petrochemical product market for poor half-year profits reported on Tuesday.
The company's current profits for the first-half of the business year ending September 30 fell 24 percent to 944 million yen ($8.28 million).
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.

"The fall in current profits can be attributed to the delay in passing rising crude prices to product wholesale prices, weak paraxylene prices and the impact of a new oil product pricing system," Hiroshi Iida, managing director of Japan Energy, told reporters.

The delay in passing on higher costs occurs because major Japanese refiners take into account the previous month's international crude oil and product prices to set the next month's oil product wholesale prices for the domestic market.
The new wholesale pricing system, introduced this year to combat imports, brings down gasoline prices while raising those of gas oil and kerosene.
However, while gasoline retail prices have fallen, there has not been a matching rise in retail prices of kerosene and gas oil, due to stiff opposition from consumers.
Paraxylene, made from naphtha, is a petrochemical product used to make polyester fibre.
The fall in current profits came despite a 9.5 percent rise in sales to 691 billion yen ($6.06 billion).
